label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To my neighbours on Aughrim Terrace,

Sorry for the letter through the door. Most of you have nothing to do with this, so apologies in advance. But one of you has been dumping your rubbish in my bin and I don't know which one, so everyone's getting it.

I'm in No. 14. Grey bin, Greenmount Bins, 14 painted on the lid in white so there's no mistaking it. It goes out Tuesday night and gets collected Wednesday morning. For the last month or so, someone has been filling it with their own bags after I put it out. Not a crisp packet or a coffee cup. Full black bags, every week.

Last Tuesday I got home from work at 3am and the lid wouldn't close. Three black bags in there that weren't mine, one of them full of nappies.

And it's costing me. Greenmount charge by weight, 41c a kilo. My bill is normally around €25 for two months. The last one was €63.20. That's the guts of 40 quid, about 90 kilos of somebody else's rubbish, paid for out of my pocket. I'm renting and I work nights behind a bar. I haven't got it to be covering anyone else's bin.

One of the bags had a gas bill envelope in it. The name had been torn off but the address was Aughrim Terrace, so I know it's someone on this road. And tearing your name off tells me you knew well what you were doing. A car was also seen pulling up at the bin on Tuesday evening.

So, to whoever it is: stop. That's all. I'm not looking for a row and I'm not going knocking on doors. I just want it to end this week.

If you're stuck, if you can't afford a bin or don't know how to go about getting one, knock in to me and I'll tell you who to ring. It's not hard, and I'd rather help than fall out with anyone. But I'm not paying for your rubbish anymore.

If it happens again, the bin gets a padlock. I work nights, I'm coming and going at all hours, and I'm not a pushover.

Thanks to everyone else for reading, and sorry again for the bother.

Your neighbour in No. 14

The 90 kilos is my sum from your numbers (the extra €38 or so divided by 41c), so it stands as long as your usual bill really is about €25.

reasons: The final sentence is a note about the calculation rather than part of the letter.
